global_organization_chain: adaptive biological trait and four tasks
coupled river ODE and ocean PDE dynamics

main_argument_chains.claim: Food-responsive sex allocation changes recruitment and resource pressure in the selected population model.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat regulation claims as scenario-bound outputs pending empirical calibration and validation.
support_steps: Fit food density to larval growth.
Couple recruitment to river and ocean states.

main_argument_chains.claim: Adaptive sex allocation creates a resistance-recovery tradeoff rather than an unconditional advantage.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Evaluate both survival under stress and time to recovery.
support_steps: Apply resource, mortality, and fecundity disturbances.
Identify delayed recovery and low-fecundity extinction risk.

main_argument_chains.claim: Ecosystem stability is evaluated by composing population trajectories, Shannon diversity, and 3-R metrics.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep metric definitions and event timing explicit before comparing interventions.
support_steps: Normalize species biomasses into Shannon S.

main_argument_chains.claim: Adding species can change which organisms benefit from variable lamprey sex allocation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not generalize until the omitted equations and parameters are recovered and validated.

main_argument_chains.claim: Host growth changes both diversity and simulated collapse timing.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Replace the local sweep with empirical global and structural sensitivity before decision use.
